newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's ups Philippines' foreign currency ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's ups Philippines' foreign currency ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it upgraded the Republic of the Philippines foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds and notes to Ba1 from Ba2.
It also raised the long-term ceiling for foreign currency bank deposits to Ba2 from Ba3.
The rating on bonds of the Republic of the Philippines was upgraded to Ba1 from Ba2, it said.
Moody's said the upgrade was supported by continued implementation of structural reforms and the considerable adjustment in fiscal accounts.
President Fidel Ramos had also placed the country on the path of sustainable growth and has substantially reduced sources of political instability, it said.

The ratings agency said prospects for continued favourable developments over the medium-term depend on the ability of the Philippines to advance further structural reforms, particularly in competing the final stage of the tax reform programme, to increase domestic savings and its role in financing investment, and to maintain appropriately tight monetary policy.
